 Asset Description : 
 A distribution lightning arrestor, also known as a metal oxide varistor (MOV) surge protector, is a device that protects electrical equipment from damage caused by lightning strikes. It's like a bouncer at a nightclub, only instead of stopping people from entering, it stops excess electricity from damaging equipment. The main components of a distribution lightning arrestor surge protector include the varistor, a high-voltage terminal, a low-voltage terminal, a ground terminal, and a bi-directional breaker. The varistor is the heart of the arrestor, and it's made of a material that can quickly dissipate excess electricity and return it to the ground. The high-voltage terminal is connected to the incoming power line, and the low-voltage terminal is connected to the equipment that the arrestor is protecting. The ground terminal is connected to the ground, and it provides a path for the excess electricity to return to the ground. The bi-directional breaker automatically trips when the excess electricity exceeds a certain level, to protect the arrestor from being damaged by high-voltage surges. The arrestor also includes an insulator, which is used to insulate the varistor from the high-voltage terminal and the low-voltage terminal, and a grounding wire, which is used to connect the ground terminal to the ground.
